newsitem.title: GERMANY: No votes to be gained by doubting the euro - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: No votes to be gained by doubting the euro - Kohl.

text.p: Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl said in remarks published on Wednesday that no votes were to be won by casting doubt on whether European monetary union (EMU) would ever come about.
Kohl's remarks in an interview with the Cologne Stadt Anzeiger daily newspaper were released ahead of publication on Thursday.
He was referring to senior opposition Social Democrats (SPD) who have cast doubt on Germany's chances of fulfilling the criteria to qualify for EMU due to be launched in 1999.
"If the Social Democrats try to make European policy into an election campaign theme we will hold out against them. The euro will come -- I have no doubt about it," Kohl said.

"The euro is more important than my own personal standing. We will create a united Europe. I shall fight for this. That is why I am standing as chancellor again in the (1998) elections," Kohl told the newspaper.

Lower Saxony state premier Gerhard Schroeder, a potential SPD candidate to challenge Kohl in next year's elections, said in an interview last week Bonn would probably have to raise taxes to meet the entry criteria for EMU.
Schroeder said he did not specifically back a delay in the planned EMU launch in 1999, but added that a rushed introduction would be more dangerous than a controlled delay.
